reason: Names keys by their physical code and reads each key's `location`: `ControlRight`, `Numpad1`, `NumpadSubtract`, `NumpadDecimal`, `NumpadEnter`, and the right-hand `location` values. Strider's key values name the key a layout types, with a left-hand Control, Shift, Alt and Meta only, and no numpad keys or `location`, so these checks have no Strider counterpart

Presses the audio and media keys (`AudioVolumeMute`, `AudioVolumeDown`, `AudioVolumeUp`, `MediaTrackNext`, `MediaTrackPrevious`, `MediaPlayPause`). Strider's named keys don't include them, so each press fails with `InvalidInput`
Reads WebKit's `keyIdentifier`, which no other browser has: the original runs it on WebKit only (`it.skip(browserName !== 'webkit')`). The port runs it on WebKit

macOS shortcuts (`Shift+Control+Alt+KeyB` selects a word, `Shift+Meta+ArrowUp` selects to the document's start) that the original runs on macOS only (`it.skip(platform !== 'darwin')`, `it.skip(!isMac)`). The harness runs on Linux, where the original skips them
